paragraphs: Here's what I think this whole passage is about, friend. Nobody gets into the kingdom of God by earning it. Jesus says, "anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it." (Mark 10:15) A child doesn't show up with a résumé. A child just holds out empty hands and receives, and that's the whole trick.

Now look at the man who ran up and knelt. He asked what he must DO to inherit eternal life, and he had a long list of things he'd done. (Mark 10:17, 20) Jesus looked at him and loved him, and then He pointed at the one thing holding the man's grip so tight, his great wealth. (Mark 10:21, 22) The man wanted to add one more thing to his list, and Jesus was offering him something to follow instead. The same goes for me and for you, baker. Anything we clutch tighter than Jesus, whether it's money, a good record or our own plans, can be the very thing in the way.

So who can be saved? The disciples asked the same thing, and Jesus answered, "With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God." (Mark 10:26, 27) That's the good news, friend. Saving us is God's work, never ours. And what He gives back is bigger than anything we let go of, and it ends in eternal life. (Mark 10:30)
